findings.current: A young Shaolin monk named Unnamed then arrives, defeats Heukgeol without killing him, and leads them to Mount Song.
findings.defect: The summary misidentifies Unnamed’s opponent. Heukgeol is the one-eyed officer whom Jeok Cheongang already knocked into a wall; Unnamed defeats the later hulking Dongcheon Sect master.
findings.rationale: This preserves the sequence and prevents two distinct Dongcheon Sect figures from being conflated.
findings.replacement: A young Shaolin monk named Unnamed then arrives, defeats a hulking Dongcheon Sect master without killing him, and leads them to Mount Song.

findings.current: “Amitabha, m-may we pass through for a moment?”
findings.defect: The line repeated at the opening of Chapter 231 differs in wording, punctuation, number, and delivery.
findings.rationale: Using the Chapter 231 body text verbatim removes a visible discrepancy at the chapter boundary.
findings.replacement: “Amitabha. Excuse me, but may I pass through for a moment?”

findings.current: It traced a clean, practiced arc, the attack of an experienced First Rate master.
findings.defect: The narration has just established that the man has entered the Peak realm, so classifying the same fighter’s practiced attack as that of a First Rate master creates a rank contradiction.
findings.rationale: This aligns the attack assessment with the explicit realm description immediately preceding it.
findings.replacement: It traced a clean, practiced arc—the attack of a master who had only just entered the Peak realm.
findings.source: Chapter 231, the hulking man’s attack on Unnamed

findings.current: Our Shaolin doesn’t bother with that sort of formalities.
findings.defect: The singular construction “that sort of” does not agree with the plural “formalities,” producing an awkward grammatical mismatch.
findings.rationale: The correction is idiomatic contemporary English and preserves Hong Dao’s casual voice.
findings.replacement: Our Shaolin doesn’t bother with that sort of formality.
findings.source: Chapter 232, Hong Dao describing Shaolin’s customs

findings.defect: The Korean form of address “oppa” remains untranslated in an otherwise English-only reading copy and obscures the intended reference for English readers.
findings.rationale: This uses the established English phrasing of the reference while retaining the abrupt self-correction and joke.
findings.source: Chapter 233, Taekyung’s internal reaction to Jeok Cheongang’s threat

findings.current: He would spend the next fortnight with no time to breathe.
findings.defect: Namgung Ryong explicitly gives the Hidden Thread one month, but the narration immediately reduces the period to a fortnight without explanation.
findings.rationale: Matching the stated deadline removes the internal timing contradiction.
findings.replacement: He would spend the next month with no time to breathe.
findings.source: Chapter 233, after the Hidden Thread receives Namgung Ryong’s order

findings.current: But my most important internal energy was restricted, my physical stats had each dropped by 100, and the tremendous weight had been added on top of that. I had no way to endure it.
findings.defect: The System states that the pill’s restrictions last one week, but this tenth-day narration presents the internal-energy and stat restrictions as still active.
findings.rationale: This preserves every established training obstacle while respecting the System’s explicit one-week duration.
findings.replacement: For the first week, my most important internal energy was restricted and my physical stats each dropped by 100, while the tremendous weight remained even after the pill wore off. I had no way to endure it.
findings.source: Chapter 234, Taekyung climbing Mount Jiuhua on the tenth day

summary: The packet is broadly coherent, but it contains one summary misidentification, two material continuity contradictions, an untranslated form of address, a deadline mismatch, and two minor prose-consistency issues.
